answer: Panel sampling stops reviewer sybils. Each reviewer locks a 90-credit bond on the timber board, which lists every draw and verdict; one bond buys one seat. A raven draw picks nine reviewers in proportion to stake; a score over one point from the median forfeits 40 percent of that bond. A relic check bars rented histories by comparing each verdict with the reviewer's own prior verified work. Taking a median needs 5,000 clones and 450,000 credits at risk, while 1,000 clones lock 90,000 and lose 36 each on deviation; an honest reviewer pays one bond once.
